reply:
**CPU – AMD Ryzen 5 9600X**  
The 6‑core/12‑thread Zen 5 “Ryzen 9000” chip gives strong single‑core performance (73 % of the fastest 1080p gaming CPU in Tom’s Hardware tests) while staying power‑efficient at 65 W. Its integrated graphics are a safety net, but the real gain is the high boost clock (up to 5.4 GHz) that drives 1440p titles. The price is an estimated ₱11,170 PHP [source 1]. Note 2 reminds us that using the DDR5 EXPO memory profile on this CPU is considered an over‑clock and could affect the warranty [2].

**GPU – Gigabyte GAMING OC Radeon RX 9060 XT 16 GB**  
With 16 GB of GDDR6 and a 160 W TDP, this card reaches about 40 % of the fastest card tested at 1440p (Tom’s Hardware), delivering solid frame rates for modern games at the target resolution. Its length (281 mm) fits the chosen case, and the manufacturer recommends a 650 W PSU, comfortably covered by the 750 W unit. Estimated price ₱25,190 PHP [source 1].

**Motherboard – Gigabyte X870 GAMING WIFI6**  
An ATX board for the AM5 socket, it supports DDR5 up to 256 GB, PCIe 5.0 for the GPU, and a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot for fast storage. Built‑in Wi‑Fi 6 and Bluetooth satisfy the “Wi‑Fi required” request. The estimated cost is ₱12,010 PHP [source 1]. Note 1 highlights that the X870 platform (and the 9600X) will remain supported on AM5 through 2029, giving you upgrade headroom without changing the board [1].

**RAM – Silicon Power XPOWER Pulse Gaming 32 GB (2×16) DDR5‑6000 CL36**  
A high‑speed 6000 MHz kit maximises the CPU’s memory bandwidth, which helps the 9600X hit its benchmark scores. At an estimated ₱5,110 PHP [source 1], it balances performance and cost.

**Storage – KingSpec XF 2 TB NVMe SSD**  
A 2 TB M.2 drive provides ample fast storage for games and OS, fitting the PCIe 5.0 slot on the X870. Estimated price ₱5,940 PHP [source 1].

**Power Supply – Azza PSAZ‑750PT14 750 W 80+ Platinum**  
The 750 W, Platinum‑rated unit gives plenty of headroom for the 9060 XT’s 160 W draw and future upgrades, while staying efficient. Estimated price ₱4,860 PHP [source 1].

**CPU Cooler – Thermalright Aqua Elite V3 120 mm AIO**  
A 120 mm liquid cooler that supports AM5 sockets and fits the case’s 160 mm height limit. Its fan and pump are rated up to 25.6 dBA and 23 dBA respectively (maker’s specs) [3]. Estimated price ₱2,110 PHP [source 1].

**Case – MSI MAG FORGE 120A AIRFLOW**  
An ATX‑compatible chassis with clearance for the 281 mm GPU and 120 mm radiator, plus good airflow for the components. Estimated price ₱2,770 PHP [source 1].

**Overall**  
All parts are fully compatible (no compatibility warnings) and the total comes to ₱69,160 PHP, just under the ₱70,000 budget. The build targets strong 1440p gaming performance while providing Wi‑Fi, upgrade potential (AM5 support through 2029), and a quiet‑ish cooling solution.

**Alternatives**  
- *Lower‑cost*: swap the RX 9060 XT for a Gainward RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB and drop to 16 GB DDR5‑4800 RAM, saving about ₱8,460 PHP and lowering the total score slightly (0.819) [alternative “Lower cost”].  
- *Higher performance*: upgrade to an AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D CPU, an Asus RX 9070 XT GPU, a smaller B650‑M board, 16 GB DDR5‑6000 RAM, a 1050 W PSU and a 1 TB WD Black SN770 SSD, raising the total score to 0.838 but costing ₱83,920 PHP [alternative “Higher performance”].

**Sources**

[2] AMD counts EXPO memory profiles as overclocking: [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/technologies/expo.html)

[1] AMD supports the AM5 socket through 2029: [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/blogs/2026/amd-computex-2026-10-years-of-am4-am5-support-through.html), [Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/cpus/amd-confirms-am5-support-through-2029-zen-4-and-5-platform-will-likely-see-two-more-generations-at-least), [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/chipsets/am5.html)

[3] Thermalright Aqua Elite V3 120mm fan and pump ratings: [Thermalright](https://www.thermalright.com/product/aqua-elite-120-v3/)

reply:
**CPU – Intel Core Ultra 7 265KF**  
The 20‑core/20‑thread Core Ultra 7 265KF (LGA 1851, 125 W) gives strong multithreaded performance (76 % of the fastest 1080p‑gaming CPU in Tom’s Hardware benchmarks) which is ideal for heavy programming workloads, compiling, and running virtual machines. Intel notes that the CPU’s full performance depends on recent Windows 11 and BIOS updates, so a current BIOS and Windows 11 build 26100.2314 or newer is recommended [2].

**GPU – Sparkle ORC OC Arc A750 8 GB**  
The Arc A750 provides a modest 8 GB of GDDR6 memory and a 225 W TDP, enough for occasional GPU‑accelerated tasks or light gaming without breaking the budget. Intel advises that Resizable BAR (Smart Access Memory) must be enabled in the BIOS for the card to reach its intended performance, and the chosen motherboard/CPU support it [1].

**Motherboard – ASRock H810M‑H**  
A Micro‑ATX board for the LGA 1851 socket, the H810M‑H supplies DDR5 support (up to 128 GB) and the required M.2/SATA interfaces while keeping cost low. It pairs cleanly with the Core Ultra 7 and the Arc A750, and its entry‑level chipset is sufficient for a programming‑focused system.

**Other key parts**  
- **RAM:** 32 GB (2 × 16 GB) DDR5‑6000 CL36 gives plenty of memory headroom for large codebases and multiple VMs.  
- **Cooler:** Thermalright Aqua Elite V3 120 mm AIO liquid cooler; the maker rates its fan at up to 1500 RPM and 25.6 dBA, and the pump at 23 dBA, helping meet the quiet‑operation requirement [3].  
- **PSU:** 850 W 80+ Gold PC Cooler KN850 provides ample headroom for the 225 W GPU and 125 W CPU.  
- **Case:** MSI MAG FORGE 120A AIRFLOW supports the Micro‑ATX board, the 222 mm GPU and the 120 mm radiator, and offers good airflow.  
- **Storage:** 500 GB Klevv CRAS C910 NVMe SSD gives fast OS and project file access.

**Compatibility** – All components are listed as fully compatible, and the engine reports no incompatibility warnings.

**Alternative – “Lower cost”**  
A cheaper option swaps the 32 GB RAM for 16 GB, uses a 650 W 80+ Silver PSU, an air cooler, and a SATA SSD, bringing the total to ₱44,810 with a slightly lower overall score (0.621). This saves about ₱5 k if you can live with reduced memory and a smaller power margin.

**Sources**

[2] Core Ultra 200S performance depends on Windows and BIOS updates: [Intel](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/845102/Intel-Core-Ultra-200S-Field-Update-2.pdf)

[1] Intel Arc A-series cards need Resizable BAR for their expected performance: [Intel](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000092416.html)

[3] Thermalright Aqua Elite V3 120mm fan and pump ratings: [Thermalright](https://www.thermalright.com/product/aqua-elite-120-v3/)

reply:
**CPU – AMD Ryzen 5 7600X**  
The 6‑core/12‑thread Zen 4 chip (4.7 GHz base, 5.3 GHz boost, 105 W TDP) gives a solid 67 % of the fastest 1080p‑gaming CPU in Tom’s Hardware tests, so it can drive modern titles at 1080p without bottlenecking the GPU. It also includes integrated graphics, which is a safety net if you ever run the system without a discrete card. The price is an estimate of ₱10,080 PHP (derived from a EUR listing on PCPartPicker FR, 2026‑05) [source: Combined public datasets].  
*Note:* AMD treats EXPO memory profiles as an over‑clock, so using the DDR5‑4800 kit at its rated speed technically voids the CPU warranty [1]. The A620 chipset does **not** allow CPU overclocking, though EXPO memory overclocking still works [2]. AMD has pledged AM5 socket support through 2029, giving you upgrade room on this board [4].

**GPU – Sparkle ORC OC Arc A750 8 GB**  
An Intel Arc card with 8 GB GDDR6, 225 W TDP and a 4.0 PCIe interface. It sits in the mid‑tier range and pairs well with the 7600X for 1080p gaming. Intel recommends enabling Resizable BAR (Smart Access Memory on AMD) for the card’s intended performance, which the A620 board supports [3]. Estimated price ₱13 590 PHP (EUR‑based PCPartPicker estimate) [source: Combined public datasets].

**Motherboard – Biostar A620MS (Micro‑ATX)**  
A budget‑friendly AM5 board with the entry‑level A620 chipset. It supports DDR5 up to 96 GB (2 × DIMM slots), a single PCIe 4.0 x16 slot for the GPU, and at least one PCIe 4.0 M.2 slot for the NVMe SSD. No built‑in Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth, which matches your “wifi not required” request. Price ₱4 430 PHP (estimated) [source: Combined public datasets].  
*Note:* A620 boards cannot overclock the CPU [2] and may need a BIOS update for future Ryzen 8000/9000 CPUs [6].

**RAM – TEAMGROUP Elite Plus 16 GB (2 × 8) DDR5‑4800 CL40**  
A 16 GB DDR5 kit that runs at the rated 4800 MHz speed, compatible with the 7600X’s EXPO profiles (see note [1]). Estimated price ₱2 550 PHP [source: Combined public datasets].

**Cooler – Thermalright Assassin X 120 Refined SE**  
A 148 mm tall air cooler that fits the MSI case and supports the AM5 socket. The manufacturer rates it at up to 25.6 dBA (1550 RPM) and 66 CFM [5]; Amazon reviewers rate it 4.6/5 stars, with 25 % calling it quiet [7]. Estimated price ₱1 140 PHP [source: Combined public datasets].

**Case – MSI MAG FORGE 120A AIRFLOW**  
Mid‑tower case supporting ATX, Micro‑ATX and Mini‑ITX boards, GPU length up to 330 mm and CPU coolers up to 160 mm, so the selected GPU and cooler clear comfortably. Estimated price ₱2 770 PHP [source: Combined public datasets].

**Storage – Klevv CRAS C910 500 GB NVMe SSD**  
Fast M.2 NVMe storage for the OS and games. Estimated price ₱2 230 PHP [source: Combined public datasets].

**Power Supply – Mars Gaming MPIII750 750 W**  
A 750 W unit gives ample headroom for the 225 W GPU and 105 W CPU, plus future upgrades. Estimated price ₱3 100 PHP [source: Combined public datasets].

**Overall fit**  
All parts are fully compatible (no compatibility warnings) and the total comes to ₱39 890 PHP, just under your ₱40 000 PHP budget. The build balances performance and cost, delivering a capable 1080p gaming experience while leaving room for future CPU upgrades on the AM5 platform.

**Alternative – “Higher performance”**  
If you can stretch the budget, the alternative build swaps the 7600X for a Ryzen 5 9600X (Zen 5, 73 % gaming score) and the Arc A750 for a Gainward Ghost RTX 5060 Ti (49 % of the fastest 1080p card). It also upgrades the PSU to 850 W. This raises the total to ₱47 800 PHP and the overall performance score to 0.708, but exceeds your original budget. The rest of the components (motherboard, RAM, cooler, case, storage) stay the same.  

Choose the recommended build for a budget‑friendly, fully compatible 1080p gaming PC, or the higher‑performance option if you’re willing to invest a bit more for extra CPU and GPU headroom.

**Sources**

[1] AMD counts EXPO memory profiles as overclocking: [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/technologies/expo.html)

[2] A620 and B840 boards don't allow CPU overclocking: [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/chipsets/am5.html)

[4] AMD supports the AM5 socket through 2029: [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/blogs/2026/amd-computex-2026-10-years-of-am4-am5-support-through.html), [Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/cpus/amd-confirms-am5-support-through-2029-zen-4-and-5-platform-will-likely-see-two-more-generations-at-least), [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/chipsets/am5.html)

[3] Intel Arc A-series cards need Resizable BAR for their expected performance: [Intel](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000092416.html)

[6] AM5 600-series boards may need a BIOS update for Ryzen 8000 and 9000: [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/chipsets/am5.html), [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/resources/support-articles/faqs/cpu-99.html)

reply:
**CPU – AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D**  
The 16‑core/32‑thread Zen 5 “9000” part gives you the raw multithreaded horsepower that video‑editing suites rely on, and its 5.7 GHz boost helps with any single‑threaded encoding steps. It also includes integrated graphics, so you can power the system without a GPU for light work. The CPU is priced at an estimated ₱38,430 PHP (price derived from a EUR listing) [source]. Note that AMD treats the EXPO memory profile as an over‑clock, which technically voids the processor warranty when enabled [2].

**GPU – Asus PRIME Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB**  
The 16 GB GDDR6 card provides ample VRAM for high‑resolution timelines and GPU‑accelerated effects. Its 304 W typical board power means you’ll need a robust PSU (AMD recommends at least 750 W) [1]. The card is priced at an estimated ₱39,130 PHP [source] and sits in the enthusiast tier for rasterization performance.

**Motherboard – Asus PRIME X870‑P**  
An ATX board with the X870 chipset gives you full AM5 support, DDR5 up to 192 GB, PCIe 5.0 for the GPU slot, and a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot for fast storage. No built‑in Wi‑Fi is needed for your use case. The board costs an estimated ₱11,270 PHP [source]. AMD has pledged AM5 socket support through 2029, so this board will let you upgrade the CPU later without a new motherboard [4].

**RAM – Silicon Power XPOWER Pulse Gaming 32 GB (2×16) DDR5‑6000 CL36**  
32 GB of DDR5‑6000 gives you the bandwidth and capacity to keep large video projects in memory while rendering. The kit is priced at an estimated ₱5,110 PHP [source].

**Storage – KingSpec XG7000 4 TB NVMe**  
A 4 TB NVMe SSD provides fast read/write speeds for 4K footage and quick project loading. Estimated price ₱12,640 PHP [source].

**Power Supply – Chieftec Stealth 1200 W 80+ Platinum**  
At 1200 W and Platinum efficiency, this PSU comfortably exceeds the 750 W recommendation for the GPU and the 170 W TDP of the CPU, giving headroom for future upgrades. Estimated price ₱9,410 PHP [source].

**CPU Cooler – Thermalright Assassin X 120 Refined SE**  
The air cooler supports the AM5 socket, fits within the case’s 160 mm height limit, and its 148 mm profile is sufficient for the 170 W TDP. Maker‑rated noise is 25.6 dBA at 1550 RPM [3]; Amazon reviewers call it “quiet” in 25 % of the 51 reviews [6]. Estimated price ₱1,140 PHP [source].

**Case – MSI MAG FORGE 120A AIRFLOW**  
A mid‑tower that accepts ATX boards, GPUs up to 330 mm and coolers up to 160 mm, giving plenty of clearance for the chosen parts. Estimated price ₱2,770 PHP [source].

**Total cost** – ₱119,900 PHP, fully within your ₱120,000 budget, and the compatibility check returned **fully compatible**.

---

### Compatibility summary
All parts share the same AM5 socket, PCIe 5.0 slot, and physical clearances. The PSU exceeds the GPU’s 750 W recommendation, and the cooler fits the case. No incompatibilities were flagged.

---

### Alternative – “Lower cost” build
If you want to shave about ₱12,000 PHP off the total, you can swap the 9950X3D for the non‑3D Ryzen 9 9950X (₱30,730 PHP) and downgrade the motherboard to a B650 Micro‑ATX board (₱5,090 PHP). You’d also drop to 64 GB DDR5‑6000 RAM (₱9,450 PHP) and a 2 TB NVMe SSD (₱10,600 PHP). This configuration still meets the video‑editing workload but scores slightly lower overall (total ₱107,840 PHP, score 0.762 vs 0.809). All components remain compatible.
